title: Start creating the interface to support true UI preferences
description:
This is step 1 of several changes that aims at treating "preferences at the UI layer that have their own files" in a generic fashion so that the code can be more unified.

Start simple by converting the language component/preference file to use the "UI preferences".

notes.body:
This was motivated by looking at the code that handles the "recent" preferences (within the -o command line option handling).  There are several "components" that can be refactored to use unified code, but I thought I'd start simple and small with just the language preference.
The goal is to eventually have all of the UI preferences hooked up to the -o command line option.

> This was motivated by looking at the code that handles the "recent" preferences

Is the difference between "preferences" and "recent"/"recent_common" that "preferences" are set through the Preferences dialog and stuff in the "recent*" files is set via other parts of the UI (View menu items, resizing by dragging, etc.), i.e. the latter are *implicitly* set as preferences and the former are *explicitly* set as references?

Unfortunately it's a mix and a mess. The "recent" have preferences with the "GUI module" so _some_ of them can be modified through the Preferences dialog, but they are marked as "obsolete" (even though they are very not obsolete), so they can have special handling at the UI layer with the -o option (see calls to recent_set_arg()) and not be written to the current preferences file.  Just some poor layering that should be corrected, and when it is will give us more flexibility on all types of preferences.  Maybe even go as far as having parts of current prefs.[c|h] in wsutil as "generic preference handling" (that's where c32147c89600bf52e93778fa4d56be0c87a666a6 is headed) with "epan layer" handling dissector preferences (and that API) and the "UI layer" handling language, profiles and "recent".

> Maybe even go as far as having parts of current prefs.\[c|h\] in wsutil as "generic preference handling" (that's where c32147c89600bf52e93778fa4d56be0c87a666a6 is headed) with "epan layer" handling dissector preferences (and that API) and the "UI layer" handling language, profiles and "recent".

That would also allow a "wiretap layer" in case preference settings would be necessary for file formats (which might represent design errors in the file format - files *should* contain all the information necessary to read them correctly - but the real world isn't always well-designed).

What do you mean by "profiles" in "language, profiles, and "recent""? A lot of epan preferences, and possibly UI preferences, are profile-dependent.

Another thing to consider is having "preferences" that are really per-conversation settings; the preference would be for the *default* setting, and the user could override them for a conversation. (A somewhat archaic example is the size of the sequence number field in LAPB, where one X.25 session might have "modulo-8" - 3-bit - sequence numbers and another one might have "modulo-128" - 7-bit - sequence numbers. We don't support modulo-128, but if we did, it should probably be per-session.)

I want common code to write "preference" files.  I consider the language, profile, recent, recent_common and preferences to all be "preference" files, but all but (epan) preferences file is written "manually". So there needs to be "preference modules" for language, profile and recent (still not sure how the "conflict" of the "gui" module name will be resolved with preferences and recent, but I'll get there), so they can use "write preference module to file" and follow a consistent format.
That should also allow something like -o:ui_language.language:french.  But hooking these new "UI preferences" to -o option will be a future MR.
